evidence_required: Probe CLIENT-STATE covers FT-003-AC-001, FT-003-AC-002, FT-003-AC-007, FT-003-AC-008, REQ-CAP-001, REQ-UX-004, REQ-REL-001 and .memory-bank/states/lifecycle-map.md#automatic-attempt-and-display. RED: before production behavior changes, the deterministic camera/ring-buffer/trigger/realtime-adapter matrix must show the absent client cannot distinguish physical/test source, form one fresh pre/post series, reject overlap, require explicit camera reselection, discard late work or preserve advertising and the 5–10-second replaceable notice across named failures. GREEN: the same seeded monotonic-clock matrix records a separate result for every referenced claim, exact state order, series identity/input dimensions, ignored trigger count, selected device behavior, stale-response rejection, notice interval/replacement and safe recovery; retain the comparison and artifact under .tasks/TASK-007-T2-FT-003-W1/.

Probe CLIENT-PROPOSALS covers FT-003-AC-004, FT-003-AC-005, REQ-CAP-002, REQ-ARCH-001 and the proposal/crop/detector claims in .memory-bank/testing/client-realtime.md#required-proof. RED: a seeded more-than-20/repeated-person plus crop-boundary fixture must fail because the accepted BlazeFace-only traversal, immediate first-20 stop, square clipping/downscale/no-upscale/metadata stripping and six-value apply-next quality behavior do not exist. GREEN: one report distinguishes traversal order and stop, repeated occurrences, every crop geometry boundary, encoded dimensions/color/metadata, every accepted/default/persisted quality value, separate versioned model delivery and negative dependency/source checks for ranking, top-5, quality gating, tracking, clustering, deduplication, embeddings, search, TensorFlow.js, YuNet and a detector abstraction.

Probe CLIENT-WIRE covers FT-003-AC-006, REQ-CAP-002 and the client-side claims in .memory-bank/contracts/realtime-attempt-api.md#multipart-serialization and #manifest-version-1. RED: a capturing fake endpoint must show the absent client cannot emit the exact manifest-first zero-to-twenty part sequence, explicit allow/omit fields, manifest-only zero case or the accepted request-manifest fields reference_series_ready_at, local_detection_completed_ms and request_started_ms. GREEN: the claim-equivalent fixture records exact part names/order/content types, strict manifest values and omissions, zero-proposal body, at-most-20/512 structural bounds and the separate wall-clock correlation plus two monotonic manifest offsets with a distinguishable pass/fail row for each referenced claim; it does not treat those manifest fields as the complete diagnostic timeline or claim server admission, QR latency or a result selection outcome.

Probe CLIENT-TIMELINE covers FT-003-AC-010, REQ-DIAG-001, REQ-PERF-001 and the client-local timing claims in .memory-bank/testing/client-realtime.md#required-proof. RED: with a seeded monotonic clock and a controlled admitted fake response delivered after request upload, the pre-change client must fail to record and correlate all three distinct moments—ready-series processing start, request-send start and response receipt—or must conflate response receipt with a request-manifest field. GREEN: the same attempt-id run records those three ordered client-local moments, compares request-to-response and ready-to-response intervals with the fixture event schedule, and retains the raw event trace plus comparison under .tasks/TASK-007-T2-FT-003-W1/; it separately records the request-manifest timing fields and stops at response receipt without implementing FT-007 diagnostic UI, Promo/QR rendering or the joint 20-attempt verdict.

Each probe runs with seeded frames, fake browser devices, a disposable browser profile and local fake endpoints, records the pre-change RED or honest pre-implementation GREEN, then claim-equivalent GREEN, and is safely rerunnable with owned cleanup. Independent /verify supplies a fresh outcome probe and VERDICT: PASS before closure.
purpose: Create the browser-local capture and proposal core that turns one accepted trigger into one fresh, structurally bounded realtime request while preserving safe advertising and client timing truth.
success_outcome: With deterministic camera, detector, sensor and realtime adapters, the central-origin browser client selects and recovers a camera, accepts one physical/test trigger path without overlap, prepares the first at most 20 chronological BlazeFace crops under the exact geometry/JPEG contract, emits the exact multipart/request-manifest timing shape, records the distinct client-local ready-series/request-send/response-receipt moments and returns safely to advertising after failure or stale work.
anti_goals: Do not implement ESP32 firmware, managed Local Network Access policy or real sensor credentials owned by TASK-008.
Do not implement central token/core Attempt persistence, realtime server admission or body enforcement owned by TASK-009.
Do not implement FT-004 search/selection, FT-005 final Promo/display acknowledgement/cooldown, FT-006 QR/session behavior or FT-007 diagnostic UI/evidence management.

Do not add a local bridge/server, WebSocket, durable trigger/outbox queue, client ranking/top-5/quality gate, tracking, clustering, deduplication, embeddings/search, YuNet, TensorFlow.js, generic detector/runtime abstraction or model OTA.

forbidden_scope: ESP32 firmware, real sensor secret provisioning and host-wide managed browser policy
Server database migrations, display-client credentials, core Attempt persistence and realtime business admission
FT-004 through FT-012 behavior and production deployment
Operator/default browser profiles, cameras, tokens, persistent data or external device mutation
stop_conditions: Execution requires changing the accepted detector, traversal, crop/JPEG, manifest, timing, state or failure-notice contract.
A browser/runtime incompatibility would require YuNet, TensorFlow.js, a bridge/local server or a generic detector/runtime abstraction.
A fresh retry or advertising-safe failure cannot be achieved without durable personalized client state or a reliable outbox.
A required RED/GREEN probe cannot run with deterministic disposable browser state and safe owned cleanup.

constraints: The accepted external/runtime owner is SpaPromoClient at expected source root clients/spa_promo_client/; its browser state owns capture/proposal preparation but no server search or result selection.

Use the smallest browser-native build/runtime arrangement compatible with the accepted MediaPipe BlazeFace browser runtime and a separately versioned model asset; exact owner-local filenames and package tooling remain implementation discretion.
Keep camera/capture window and maximum input dimensions deployment-configured, downscale before ring-buffer/detector work and never turn exact site values into a task gate.
Represent sensor and realtime as narrow deterministic adapters in this task so real authentication/deployment can be added by later tasks without changing the state/proposal core.
The client may persist only accepted kiosk-profile configuration such as camera identity and JPEG quality; active frames, personalized result and Attempt state remain discardable browser memory.
invariants: Physical and test sources enter one trigger path but remain distinguishable; busy states never create overlapping capture and every retry uses a fresh series.
Chronological traversal stops immediately at occurrence 20 and preserves detector order; repeated occurrences remain valid.
Crops follow the exact clipped square, no-alignment, no-upscale, 512-pixel and metadata-free JPEG contract, and quality changes apply only from the next Attempt.
The manifest never contains spa_id, a token/secret, camera label/config snapshot, bbox/crop/source dimensions or occurrence UUID.
Failure or stale work cannot replace the current display state; the loaded client retains usable advertising and no success cooldown begins.
verification_targets: CLIENT-STATE -> FT-003-AC-001, FT-003-AC-002, FT-003-AC-007, FT-003-AC-008, REQ-CAP-001, REQ-UX-004 and REQ-REL-001 with separate trigger, camera, stale-work, retry, advertising and notice results.
CLIENT-PROPOSALS -> FT-003-AC-004, FT-003-AC-005, REQ-CAP-002 and REQ-ARCH-001 with separate traversal, detector delivery, crop/JPEG, quality and forbidden-authority results.
CLIENT-WIRE -> FT-003-AC-006 and REQ-CAP-002 with separate multipart, zero-proposal, structural-bound and request-manifest timing-field results.
CLIENT-TIMELINE -> FT-003-AC-010, REQ-DIAG-001 and REQ-PERF-001 with separate ready-series processing-start, request-send-start, response-receipt, ordering, correlation and interval results.
